traps.shape: GraphQL asset import from a caller-supplied URL whose host is a loopback literal, resolves to loopback, or carries a credentials component in front of a loopback host
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Asset mutations are gated by an explicitly granted GraphQL schema action (volumes.<uid>.create/save), so the caller is treated as a trusted API consumer.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code (the advisory's own route)

traps.shape: control-panel resource action derives its allowed resource origin from the request Host, so a spoofed Host makes the base URL itself attacker-chosen and the action fetches the internal host
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The action already rejects URLs that do not start with the control-panel resource base URL and requires a control-panel request, so it looks origin-locked.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fixes never touch this file

traps.shape: the resource action follows a redirect from the resource origin to a different origin/address without revalidating the destination, so the first-hop check never sees the address actually contacted
traps.reason_to_dismiss: Redirects are normal HTTP behaviour, and the URL that was supplied and validated is assumed to be the URL that is fetched.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the client sets no redirect policy

traps.shape: an operator-configured loopback dev-server probe through the shared HTTP client must keep working; a blanket address guard on that client silently disables it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The dev-server probe is dev-only tooling that must reach a loopback dev server; it is not attacker-controlled.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the probe is a coupled value next to the shared client
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a: coupled value, covered by functional/06_dev_server_probe.php
